anatomy.flutter: Single Breadcrumb({items: List<BreadcrumbEntry>}) widget: takes a data list of BreadcrumbEntry.link(label, onTap)/BreadcrumbEntry.page(label) and derives separators itself, rendering into one Semantics(container:true, label:'breadcrumb') + Wrap; there is no separate exported Breadcrumb/BreadcrumbList/BreadcrumbItem/BreadcrumbLink/BreadcrumbPage/BreadcrumbSeparator/BreadcrumbEllipsis composition API -- those are internal (_Crumb, ExcludeSemantics+Icon inline).
anatomy.web: Seven separately exported pieces a caller composes by hand: Breadcrumb (nav), BreadcrumbList (ol), BreadcrumbItem (li), BreadcrumbLink (a, asChild-capable), BreadcrumbPage (span, aria-current=page), BreadcrumbSeparator (li, defaults to a ChevronRightIcon child but accepts children override), BreadcrumbEllipsis (span with sr-only 'More' text).
anatomy.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The port deliberately collapses the reference's seven-part composable API into one data-driven widget (Breadcrumb(items: [...])), per its own doc comment: 'The reference writes each BreadcrumbSeparator out by hand... so the port derives them rather than making the caller interleave two kinds of thing into one list. A caller cannot express two crumbs with no separator, which the reference never asks for.' That is a real anatomy gap even though it is a documented, deliberate simplification: a Flutter caller cannot override a separator's content (no chevron replacement), cannot omit a separator between two adjacent crumbs, and has no BreadcrumbEllipsis equivalent at all -- the Flutter file exports no ellipsis widget, while breadcrumb.tsx does (lines 93-113), even though (per the Flutter doc) the web's own reference page never mounts one either.

api.flutter: BreadcrumbEntry.link(label, {onTap}) / BreadcrumbEntry.page(label) -- two-variant sealed data shape, isPage bool, no separate href string (onTap is a VoidCallback since the reference's own links point at '#').
api.web: BreadcrumbLink accepts asChild + arbitrary <a> props (href, target, etc.); BreadcrumbSeparator accepts children to override the default chevron; BreadcrumbEllipsis is its own exported component with a fixed size-5/size-4 icon and sr-only 'More' label.

ORIGINAL: BreadcrumbEllipsis exists on the web (exported, collapsed-trail affordance) but has no Flutter counterpart at all -- 'BreadcrumbEllipsis is recorded, not built' per the Dart file's own library doc, meaning a Flutter consumer needing a collapsed/overflow trail has nothing to reach for. This is a genuine, self-acknowledged API gap, not a platform difference, since nothing about Flutter prevents building the widget -- it was simply not built because the reference page never renders one.

states.flutter: A link crumb (_Crumb, non-page) runs a TweenAnimationBuilder<Color?> from mutedForeground to foreground on hover, driven by Press's onHoverChange, at MotionDurations.normal on MotionCurves.enter (250ms ease-out) -- the current-page crumb never changes colour and is marked enabled:false.
states.web: BreadcrumbLink declares `transition-colors hover:text-foreground` (measured 0.25s --ease-out, muted-foreground -> foreground); BreadcrumbPage is `font-normal text-foreground` with no hover rule and role="link" aria-disabled="true" aria-current="page".

disabled.flutter: BreadcrumbEntry.page renders via Semantics(link: true, enabled: false, ...) -- the current-page crumb is explicitly not interactive, with no visual disabled treatment because it was never a pressable control to begin with (plain StyledText, no Press wrapper).
disabled.web: BreadcrumbPage carries role="link" aria-disabled="true" aria-current="page" and is a <span>, not an <a> -- never clickable, with no opacity/disabled styling since it renders as ordinary text.

interaction.flutter: Link crumbs are wrapped in Press(link: true, onTap, semanticLabel, onHoverChange, focusRadius: Radii.sm) -- the doc comment states Press supplies 'Tab reachability, Enter and Space, the click cursor, a focus ring, a name, and a 44px target under a 20px-tall word', matching keyboard activation and a target-size floor; separators are ExcludeSemantics-wrapped so they are inert to both pointer and screen reader.
interaction.web: BreadcrumbLink renders a real <a> (keyboard-focusable and Enter-activatable natively); BreadcrumbSeparator carries role="presentation" aria-hidden="true" so it is excluded from the accessibility tree and, being an <li> with no tabindex, from keyboard traversal too.

semantics.flutter: Semantics(container: true, label: 'breadcrumb', explicitChildNodes: true) wraps the whole trail (port of aria-label="breadcrumb" on <nav>); the separator icon is ExcludeSemantics-wrapped (port of role="presentation" aria-hidden="true").
semantics.web: <nav aria-label="breadcrumb">; BreadcrumbSeparator carries role="presentation" aria-hidden="true"; BreadcrumbEllipsis carries role="presentation" aria-hidden="true" plus a visible sr-only "More" span for the icon-only button it decorates.
